title: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: New 15% DEI tax tier
sections.summary: The first amendments add a 15% concessionary tax rate tier for the Development and Expansion Incentive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The first set of amendments introduces an additional concessionary tax rate tier of 15% for the Development and Expansion Incentive (DEI).

sections.label: Clause 2 DEI tax tier
sections.summary: Clause 2 introduces a new 15% concessionary tax rate tier under the DEI and applies other DEI features to it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 2 introduces a new concessionary tax rate tier of 15% under the DEI and provides for other features of the DEI to be applied to the new 15% tax rate tier.

sections.label: Eligible companies and 40-year tenure
sections.summary: Clause 3 expands eligible companies for a DEI award tenure of up to 40 years and extends the sub-scheme to 31 December 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Some examples of companies that could benefit from this expansion are those that provide payment technologies and solutions or artificial intelligence (AI) solutions and aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Then, clause 3 expands the scope of companies eligible for a DEI award tenure of up to 40 years and extends this sub-scheme up to 31 December 2028.

sections.label: 15% floor for large MNEs
sections.summary: A multilateral commitment imposes a 15% floor on effective tax rates for large multinational enterprises with annual group revenue of $750 million or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The multilateral commitment to impose a 15% floor on effective tax rates for large multinational enterprises (MNEs), groups with annual group revenue of $750 million or more in at least two of the four preceding financial years, will restrict tax competition and reshape the manner in which countries will have to compete for foreign direct investment (FDI), and the jobs and stimulus that come with FDI.

sections.label: New 15% certificate tier
sections.summary: The amendment Bill introduces a new tier where a 15% concessionary tax rate can be granted in the certificate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendment Bill will also introduce a new tier where a 15% concessionary tax rate can be granted in the certificate.

sections.label: Investment Allowance Scheme change
sections.summary: The amendment Bill's other main change concerns the Investment Allowance Scheme, which allows tax exemption of up to 100% of fixed capital expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The other main change under this amendment Bill relates to the Investment Allowance Scheme, under which businesses can enjoy a tax exemption of up to 100% of fixed capital expenditure incurred.

sections.label: Businesses paid lower tax rates
sections.summary: Businesses on average paid 5.1% in that year and 4.3% in 2019, less than a third of that.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Businesses, on average, however, paid less than a third of that: 5.1% in that year and an even lower 4.3% in 2019.

sections.label: Section 22 tax treatment limit
sections.summary: Amendments to section 22 propose limiting the favourable tax treatment to five years, through the end of 2028.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, the amendments to section 22 propose to limit the favourable tax treatment to five years, through to the end of 2028.

sections.label: DEI extension or 2028 sunset
sections.summary: Clause 2J suggests DEIs have been in place since 2012, and the House should understand if there might be another extension or adherence to 2028.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I will note that in the Bill, in clause 2J, it seems to suggest that DEIs have been in place since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It will be useful for this House to understand if there might yet again be an extension of the DEI for qualifying firms, or if the Government will, indeed, commit to adhering to the 2028 date as a genuine sunset.

sections.label: Conditions for 5% tax rate
sections.summary: To qualify for a 5% tax rate, a firm must expend an additional $13 million in fixed asset investment and employ 30 more skilled employees by the fifth year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, to qualify for a tax rate of 5% in the former, a firm must expend an additional $13 million in fixed asset investment and employ an additional 30 skilled employees by the fifth year.

sections.label: ETR for SMEs and corporations
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance previously stated the ETR for SMEs over the past decade runs between 4% and 5%, while larger corporations amounted to between 10% and 11%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To be clear, the Minister for Finance had, in response to Parliamentary Questions filed by my hon friend, Louis Chua, previously stated that the ETR for SMEs over the past decade runs between 4% and 5%, while that for larger corporations amounted to between 10% and 11%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While one may take issue with the precise way that this calculation is made, my sense is that the combination of BEPS-related stipulations embedded in last month's Bills, alongside the Bill that we are debating today, will go a significant way towards redressing any residual bias in favour of granting large corporations excessively generous tax relief.

sections.label: Additional 15% concessionary tax rate
sections.summary: The Bill introduces an additional 15% concessionary tax rate for certain qualifying income, alongside existing 5% and 10% rates for the DEI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces an additional 15% concessionary tax rate for certain qualifying income, alongside existing 5% and 10% rates for the DEI.

sections.label: Switching between base rates
sections.summary: The amendment lets companies switch between 5%, 10% and 15% base rates and corresponding stepped-up rates, subject to eligibility criteria, giving flexibility over the tax relief period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment also allows companies to switch between the 5%, 10% and 15% base rates and their corresponding stepped-up rates, subject to eligibility criteria, thus allowing flexibility to these companies in managing their tax burden over the tax relief period.

sections.label: Extended DEI tax relief periods
sections.summary: Tax relief periods for DEI recipients may now be extended up to 31 December 2028, potentially benefiting companies with longer project timelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Tax relief periods for DEI recipients may now be extended up to 31 December 2028, potentially benefiting companies with longer project timelines.

sections.label: Key DEI enhancements
sections.summary: Key enhancements include an additional layer of concessionary tax rates aligned with BEPS 2.0 global tax standards, extended tax relief, a revised fixed asset investment definition and expanded qualifying activities under DEI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Key enhancements include an additional layer of concessionary tax rates aligned with global tax standards introduced by BEPS 2.0; extended tax relief; a revised definition of fixed asset investment; and an expanded scope of qualifying activities under DEI.

sections.label: Clause 4 investment allowances
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends sections 41 and 43 on investment allowances, broadening the definition of fixed capital expenditure to support companies developing and expanding capabilities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, clause 4 amends sections 41 and 43 on investment allowances, broadening the definition of fixed capital expenditure to support companies developing and expanding capabilities in Singapore.

sections.label: Fixed capital expenditure definition expanded
sections.summary: Expanding the definition of fixed capital expenditure to include acquisition of know-how or patent rights can attract projects where commercialisation or industrialisation builds on acquired intellectual properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Expanding the definition of fixed capital expenditure to include the acquisition of know-how or patent rights, can also attract projects where commercialisation or industrialisation builds on acquired intellectual properties (IPs).

sections.label: DEI concessionary tax rate eligibility
sections.summary: The DEI 5% and DEI 10% concessionary tax rate tier will be available to all eligible companies, regardless of country of origin, company size or Pillar Two scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The DEI 5% and DEI 10% concessionary tax rate tier will be available to all eligible companies, regardless of their country of origin, the size of the company or whether they are in scope of Pillar Two.

sections.label: No unilateral tax rate changes
sections.summary: The Government will not unilaterally amend a company's concessionary tax rate if it continues to meet its incentive outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In fact, in line with upholding Singapore's reputation as a trusted and transparent business hub and as a general principle, the Government will not unilaterally amend a company's concessionary tax rate if it continues to meet its incentive outcome.

sections.label: DEI take-up fluctuates
sections.summary: DEI take-up fluctuates yearly, with a mix of DEI 5% and DEI 10%, the latter forming the bulk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The take-up of DEI fluctuates from year to year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: There is a good mix of both DEI 5% and DEI 10%, with DEI 10% making the bulk of this mix.

sections.label: DEI extension to 2028
sections.summary: The DEI extension to 31 December 2028 refers to its limited scope allowing up to 40-year tenure for service companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The extension of the DEI for another five years to 31 December 2028 is, in fact, in reference to the limited scope of DEI that allows for a DEI tenure of up to 40 years for headquarter and non-headquarter service companies.

sections.label: Tax forgone is notional
sections.summary: Tax forgone from awarding DEI tax incentives is considered notional in nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To Mr Saktiandi Supaat's question on corporate tax income "forgone" under DEI, a point that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also raised, we consider any tax forgone by the award of the tax incentives to be notional in nature.

sections.label: Pillar Two reduces incentive effectiveness
sections.summary: Pillar Two of BEPS 2.0 reduces certain tax incentives' effectiveness, as MNEs with revenues of at least €750 million face a 15% minimum effective tax rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat rightly pointed out that the implementation of Pillar Two of BEPS 2.0 would reduce the effectiveness of certain tax incentives, since MNEs with consolidated annual revenues of at least €750 million will be subject to a minimum effective tax rate of 15% wherever they operate.

sections.label: No EEIA overhaul plans
sections.summary: The Refundable Investment Credit scheme is a recent example, and there are no current plans to overhaul the EEIA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The new Refundable Investment Credit scheme, which was debated last month here in Parliament, is one recent example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We have no plans currently to overhaul the EEIA at the moment, but I note the Member's feedback to consider a new consolidated Act.

sections.label: Incentives for manufacturing and services
sections.summary: Incentive requirements must reflect differences between manufacturing and services, and Investment Allowance is given for new substantive projects aligned with economic priorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And our incentive requirements must therefore also reflect the differences between manufacturing as well as the services sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I want to ensure the Member that the Investment Allowance is given with respect to new substantive projects that our economic agencies have assessed to be in line with our economic priorities.

sections.label: Government non-tax advantages investment
sections.summary: The Government will continue to invest in non-tax, non-incentive advantages such as an educated workforce, infrastructure, connectivity, legal system and financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Government will continue to invest in our non-tax, non-incentive advantages such as a highly educated workforce and talent pool, our robust infrastructure, our excellent connectivity, a well-established legal system and a well-developed financial system.

sections.label: DEI assessment and negotiation flexibility
sections.summary: Economic agencies assess the DEI based on commitments, and the Bill provides flexibility for negotiation amid external and economic changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For the DEI, as I mentioned, the economic agencies will assess that based on all of the different commitments and it has to be commensurate to those commitments under the qualifying activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And again, the whole Bill was meant to ensure flexibility, so that, for example, if there are changes to the external environment, changes to the investment climate, the economic climate, it gives the economic agencies as well as the company itself, scope to negotiate and say, "Well, I am at this tier now, I can do more".

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Or the company can say, "Oh, it's a bit challenging, I need more time".

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, that flexibility gives companies some certainty and it also allows for economic agencies to work closely with companies to invest in Singapore.
